primitives.name: Bradley-Terry Pairwise Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: hJudge-8B distilled from Claude Opus 4.6 teacher: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, LoRA rank 16, scale 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, batch 8, cosine schedule, 2 epochs, ~50 min on one 80 GB A100.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(i \\succ j)': 'probability that model i beats model j', '\\sigma': 'logistic function', '\\theta_i, \\theta_j': 'latent skill parameters for models i and j'}
primitives.assumptions: Model preferences are transitive; judge responses follow Bradley-Terry distribution; pairwise comparisons are independent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When θi ≈ θj, P(i≻j) approaches 0.5, indicating indistinguishable performance.

layer2.mapping: The Bradley-Terry model mirrors GSI's team-rating system where each team's latent strength is inferred from pairwise match outcomes, with logits representing relative dominance.
layer2.telemetry: Leaderboard scores and confidence intervals derived from pairwise judgments.

primitives.name: Replayable Trajectory Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Report two deterministic validity measures: renderable (loads cleanly, non-blank screenshot) and replayable (renderable + schema-valid trajectory, all actions execute, screenshots captured).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'renderable': 'binary indicator (1 if valid, 0 otherwise)', 'replayable': 'binary indicator (1 if valid, 0 otherwise)'}
primitives.assumptions: Interaction trajectories are executable and verifiable through browser automation; visual fidelity is captured via screenshot comparison.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When trajectory fails execution or deviates from expected component changes, validation fails.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, this kernel enables automated QA workflows where model-generated UI walkthroughs are replayed to detect regressions or logical inconsistencies before deployment.
layer2.telemetry: Render rate and replay rate percentages across candidate dashboards.

primitives.name: Trajectory Analytical Coverage
primitives.verbatim_quote: (4) VLM pairwise judge takes task + schema + screenshots + execution reports → structured A/B/tie preference with rationale.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'analytical_coverage': 'dimensionless score quantifying depth of analytical intent covered by trajectory'}
primitives.assumptions: Analytical intent is encoded in natural language and mapped to actionable components; coverage reflects true interpretability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low coverage indicates shallow or irrelevant interaction paths; high coverage implies rich exploratory analytics.

layer2.mapping: GSI uses trajectory coverage to evaluate how well a model's dashboard supports complex analytical queries—key for predictive modeling of team performance.
layer2.telemetry: Average coverage scores per model across all tasks.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of DashArena lies in its dual validation framework: deterministic rendering and replayability ensure technical correctness, while analytical coverage ensures semantic richness. The Bradley-Terry model provides a principled way to aggregate these heterogeneous signals into a coherent ranking. In GSI, this translates to treating each team’s rating as a latent variable influenced by pairwise match outcomes, with trajectory-based metrics serving as proxies for analytical sophistication. For GSE, the replayable trajectory becomes a formalized QA protocol, allowing simulation of user journeys to validate UI logic before release. The failure mode occurs when models generate technically correct but semantically vacuous dashboards—this manifests as high render rates but low analytical coverage, which the Bradley-Terry model mitigates by incorporating human judgment.
